Topics · Is there a God?

Did religion just evolve in the human brain?

The science stands as an account of how belief forms. Whether belief is true it does not say, either way.

Part 1 of 3

﴿فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفًا ۚ فِطْرَتَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِى فَطَرَ ٱلنَّاسَ عَلَيْهَا ۚ لَا تَبْدِيلَ لِخَلْقِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلْقَيِّمُ وَلَـٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

So direct your face [i.e., self] toward the religion, inclining to truth. [Adhere to] the fiṭrah[1145] of Allāh upon which He has created [all] people. No change should there be in the creation of Allāh.[1146] That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know.

Translator's notes

[1145] The natural inborn inclination of man to worship his Creator prior to the corruption of his nature by external influences. Thus, Islāmic monotheism is described as the religion of fiṭrah - that of the inherent nature of mankind. [1146] i.e., let people remain true to their fiṭrah within the religion of Islām.

Quran · Ar-Rum 30:30

Translation

(for when Gentiles who don’t have the law do by nature the things of the law, these, not having the law, are a law to themselves, in that they show the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience testifying with them, and their thoughts among themselves accusing or else excusing them)

Original · Ancient Greek

ὅταν γὰρ ἔθνη τὰ μὴ νόμον ἔχοντα φύσει τὰ τοῦ νόμου ποιῶσιν, οὗτοι νόμον μὴ ἔχοντες ἑαυτοῖς εἰσιν νόμος· οἵτινες ἐνδείκνυνται τὸ ἔργον τοῦ νόμου γραπτὸν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν, συμμαρτυρούσης αὐτῶν τῆς συνειδήσεως καὶ μεταξὺ ἀλλήλων τῶν λογισμῶν κατηγορούντων ἢ καὶ ἀπολογουμένων,

Romans · 2:14-15

World English Bible

Accept the findings. Humans detect agents readily, see purpose in nature, and take easily to the idea of unseen minds. Children do this with little teaching, across cultures. Two readings fit those facts. One: these are by-products of minds shaped for survival, and they point at nothing. Two: people are disposed to this because there is something for it to point at. This text makes the second claim. It says the disposition is built in. The data do not decide between them.

A question for you

Which reading is closer to yours right now?

If you sayA by-product that points at nothing.
ThenThat is a serious position. It needs one more step: that the origin shows falsehood. That comes next.
If you sayA tendency that points at something real.
ThenThat is possible, and the science does not establish it. It has other arguments.
If you sayI don't know, and I don't think the data can say.
ThenThat is what this argument says too.

Part 2 of 3

Original · Hebrew

יְהוָ֞ה עֻזִּ֧י וּמָעֻזִּ֛י וּמְנוּסִ֖י בְּי֣וֹם צָרָ֑ה אֵלֶ֗יךָ גּוֹיִ֤ם יָבֹ֨אוּ֙ מֵֽאַפְסֵי־אָ֔רֶץ וְיֹאמְר֗וּ אַךְ־שֶׁ֨קֶר֙ נָחֲל֣וּ אֲבוֹתֵ֔ינוּ הֶ֖בֶל וְאֵֽין־בָּ֥ם מוֹעִֽיל׃ הֲיַעֲשֶׂה־לּ֥וֹ אָדָ֖ם אֱלֹהִ֑ים וְהֵ֖מָּה לֹ֥א אֱלֹהִֽים׃

Jeremiah · 16:19-20

World English Bible

Does explaining a belief defeat it? The origin of a belief does not by itself decide its truth. Your belief in evolution has a psychological and social history too. But the debunker's argument is sharper: if a process would have produced this belief whether or not it were true, the belief has lost its support. Fair. The verse quotes people saying that they found their fathers on a path. Inheritance alone is not offered there as proof.

A question for you

When does explaining a belief weaken the belief?

If you sayWhen the cause has nothing to do with the truth.
ThenThat is a strict standard. It remains to ask whether it applies here, and whether it applies to reason itself.
If you sayNever. Origin is one thing, truth another.
ThenThat is too strong. Someone who learns that their clock has stopped should not trust it, even if it happens to be right.
If you sayWhen a simpler explanation is available.
ThenThat is a reasonable standard. The question is what the simpler account explains, and what it does not.

Quran · Al-Isra 17:36

Translation

I tell you that every idle word that men speak, they will give account of it in the day of judgment. For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.”

Original · Ancient Greek

λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶν ῥῆμα ἀργὸν ὃ λαλήσουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, ἀποδώσουσιν περὶ αὐτοῦ λόγον ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως· ἐκ γὰρ τῶν λόγων σου δικαιωθήσῃ, καὶ ἐκ τῶν λόγων σου καταδικασθήσῃ.

the Gospel (Matthew) · 12:36-37

World English Bible

A warning on this app's own argument. Elsewhere it asks: if reason evolved to survive, why trust it on truth? That is the debunker's argument aimed the other way; it cannot use one and refuse the other. Survival origins raise a real question for any capacity. Reasoning has independent checks: prediction, proof, success. Belief in God has evidence of another kind: the world's order, conscience, the message. So the cases differ, and the app says so. The verse sets one standard: do not follow what you have no knowledge of.

A question for you

What do you take from this warning?

If you sayOrigin arguments work for neither side.
ThenThen the matter returns to the reasons themselves, not the belief's origin.
If you sayThey work better against religion.
ThenMany hold that view. It remains whether it reaches falsehood or only caution, and whether belief's own evidence answers it.
If you sayI want to see the other argument.
ThenHere it is.

The same in the other books

In the body restraint is good, good is restraint in speech, in thought restraint is good, good is restraint in all things. A Bhikshu, restrained in all things, is freed from all pain.
